title: Scientific Opinion on Dietary Reference Values for vitamin C
authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the European Commission (question EFSA-Q-2011-01229).
result: Vitamin C is an essential component of the diet, as humans and other primates have lost the ability to synthesise it. It is a cofactor of monooxygenases, dioxygenases and mixed function oxygenases, reducing the active-centre metal ion and maintaining it in a reduced state. Procollagen-proline dioxygenase and procollagen-lysine 5-dioxygenase require vitamin C for maximal activity, and deficiency impairs the synthesis of collagen, the principal protein of skin, bones, teeth and connective tissues. Scurvy occurs in adults at a plasma ascorbate below 10 umol/L and a body pool below 300 mg, with tooth loss, joint pain, poor wound healing, petechiae, bruising and inflamed, bleeding gums; an intake of 10 mg/day prevents it.
